sources.title_iast: Thousand Ways to the Transcendental: reviewed inline Sanskrit analysis
sources.witness: Closed-population inventory and review map for every Sanskrit occurrence remaining inside Chinmayananda prose after standalone quotations are promoted. Each unique unit resolves either to an exact reviewed name/quotation analysis or to an independently derived popup checked against the shared Prakriya grammatical-text witnesses; the unfinished interpreter was not used.
sources.notes: The marked-script inventory contains 2,753 occurrences representing 750 unique units: 146 exact references to existing reviewed analysis and 604 independent popups. The tokenizer treats ñ-bearing forms such as yajña, prajñānam, and kṣetrajñaḥ as whole words. English components joined to Sanskrit by OCR-style hyphens stay ordinary prose and are never invented as Sanskrit words. Validation requires exact source offsets, complete population replay, clean lexical glosses, and a matching primary/raw Dhātupāṭha witness for every recorded root locus. The public UI presents the supported grammar without adding an agreement/disagreement verdict about Chinmayananda's prose.

sources.title_iast: Thousand Ways to the Transcendental: reviewed undiacritized Roman Sanskrit

sources.notes: All 1,267 locator candidates are adjudicated: 1,246 Sanskrit occurrences and 21 English/citation-label false positives. The accepted population has 126 exact reviewed references and 1,120 independent popups. Of the accepted occurrences, 1,073 render as prose popups and 173 are already represented by a structured Sanskrit/Gītā block. Cross-review rejected generic morphology, rootless verbal forms, fabricated prefixed roots, silent homonym substitution, empty evidence, and English plurals presented as Sanskrit inflections.

sources.witness: Closed 56-unit packet extracted from paired Muktābodha M00351 Devanāgarī and IAST transcriptions of Vāsudeva Śarmā Paṇaśīkara's Nirṇaya Sāgar edition, checked directly against printed pages 302–309 in the 1937 scan. The packet carries parallel readings from the 2012 historical-critical Mokṣopāya Sthitiprakaraṇa and the repository Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha vulgate witness.
sources.notes: Gauḍa Abhinanda, associated with the Laghu-Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha, is not the South-Indian Krama author represented by the existing abhinanda thinker ID. The controlling public sequence preserves the printed mīmabhāsa- reading at 2.33 rather than silently emending it. The attached apparatus records critical yantrapuruṣāḥ at MU 4.9.38 against the later received Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha's atyajñapuruṣāḥ at 4.27.38 and the longer construction cluster at MU 4.7.34–39. ‘Vulgate’ means the commonly received and printed expanded text, not a judgment of spiritual worth. Swami Venkatesananda's Supreme Yoga is a faithful chapter-summary that freely translates one selected verse per chapter: its ‘robot-like working projections’ is an interpretive compression of the whole artificial-production and automatic-action account, not a direct translation of an explicit yantrapuruṣa token in that later witness. The critical Mokṣopāya independently supports the interpretation.
